title: Andrew Yang 楊安澤
content_html:
Andrew Yang is an American entrepreneur, author, and politician born on January 13, 1975, in Schenectady, New York, to parents who immigrated from Taiwan. He holds a B.A. from Brown University and a J.D. from Columbia Law School. After a brief stint as a corporate attorney, he became CEO of Manhattan Prep before founding Venture for America in 2011, a nonprofit fellowship placing recent college graduates in startups in emerging cities. He was named a White House Champion of Change by the Obama administration in 2012 for this work.

Yang ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2020, gaining national attention for his advocacy of Universal Basic Income — a policy he called the “Freedom Dividend” of $1,000 per month to every American adult. His campaign, backed by a grassroots following known as the “Yang Gang,” helped bring UBI into mainstream political discourse. He withdrew from the race in February 2020 and subsequently ran for Mayor of New York City in 2021.

In 2021, Yang founded the Forward Party, a centrist third-party political organization aimed at breaking what he describes as the dysfunction of the two-party system. He has authored three books, including The War on Normal People (2018), which laid out his economic arguments for UBI, and Forward (2021), which makes the case for political realignment.
